question: What maintained filesystem boundary should OpenClaw expose: a rule-based `tools.fs` allow/deny policy, workspace-only plus external sandboxing, or a split file-tools policy with exec tracked separately?
rationale: This adds a new config contract and security boundary across tool families, and the active PathGuard branch deliberately excludes arbitrary shell execution while current behavior preserves unrestricted host filesystem access by default.

options.title: Design core tools.fs policy
options.body: Adopt a versioned `tools.fs` allow/deny contract for file/media/apply_patch paths and require docs/tests to state whether exec is covered or separately tracked.

options.title: Split exec explicitly
options.body: Allow a file-tools-only implementation only if it documents the exec gap and links the exec path policy to a separate canonical issue before presenting the feature as sandboxing.

options.title: Keep workspaceOnly only
options.body: Decline path-level config for now and direct operators to Docker, OS-user isolation, current `workspaceOnly`, and tool deny policies.

recommendation.title: Design core tools.fs policy
recommendation.body: Adopt a versioned `tools.fs` allow/deny contract for file/media/apply_patch paths and require docs/tests to state whether exec is covered or separately tracked.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest routing signal from the original workspace-only guard, adjacent security/path work, and prior review on this exact issue.
